categories.name: Agent Security & Trust Boundaries
categories.summary: A dominant theme emerged around treating AI agents as untrusted components requiring systems-level security controls rather than relying on model robustness alone. Multiple papers and articles emphasized that agent security failures map to classic systems-security principles: least privilege, complete mediation, and instruction/data separation. The shift from sandboxed evals to real-world privilege analysis and the emergence of frameworks like CIK (Capability/Identity/Knowledge) taxonomy reflect maturing threat models for agentic deployments.

key_items.title: Agent security requires systems thinking, not model fixes
key_items.detail: CSO coverage of research mapping 11 real agent attacks to systems-security failures argues for treating the model as untrusted and enforcing controls externally.

key_items.title: OpenClaw safety analysis with CIK taxonomy
key_items.detail: Paper introduces Capability/Identity/Knowledge framework and tests 12 live attack scenarios against agents with broad local and service privileges.

key_items.title: Shadow agents expand endpoint attack surface
key_items.detail: Cyberhaven guidance recommends treating agents like endpoint apps with inventory, permission constraints, and OS/network-level egress controls.

key_items.title: Auto-policy vs auto-skill gap in physical agents
key_items.detail: Research highlights that scaling auto-generated skills without external policy enforcement widens tool-to-action trust boundaries in IoT workflows.

categories.name: MCP Security & Supply Chain
categories.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) emerged as a critical attack surface with multiple advisories and research papers addressing SSRF vulnerabilities, skill/connector trust boundaries, and supply chain risks. The consensus is that MCP deployments require end-to-end controls: URL allowlists, connector authentication, tool permission constraints, and data-leakage monitoring around MCP servers.

key_items.title: MCP SSRF vulnerability in Anthropic and Microsoft tools
key_items.detail: Full Disclosure advisory describes prompt-injection-driven SSRF chain exposing IAM credentials via cloud metadata endpoints; mitigations include RFC1918 blocking and IMDSv2.

key_items.title: SkillSpector scans agent skills pre-deployment
key_items.detail: Scanner checks for prompt injection, metadata poisoning, permission mismatch, tool misuse, and vulnerable packages with SARIF-ready output.

key_items.title: MCP Security hardening guide from Strac
key_items.detail: Comprehensive framing for securing MCP servers, connectors, and data flows with authentication, permission constraints, and supply-chain checks.

key_items.title: Agent Skills architecture and security path forward
key_items.detail: Paper examines how trust boundaries shift from model weights to skill acquisition/runtime layers as agents load instructions/code on demand.

categories.name: Prompt Injection & LLM Exploitation
categories.summary: Prompt injection continues to be validated as a high-impact attack vector across diverse contexts including academic peer review, coding assistants, and agent skill packages. Research demonstrated that invisible-font injections can steer LLM reviewer scores to acceptance levels, and that coding agents can be weaponized as attacker shells through unvetted external artifacts.

key_items.title: LLM-as-Reviewer benchmark exposes injection risks
key_items.detail: Study of 12 LLMs on 898 papers shows hidden instructions can steer review scores; recommends input sanitization and out-of-band verification.

key_items.title: Agentic coding assistants become attacker shells
key_items.detail: Research shows how hidden prompt-injection in external artifacts crosses trust boundaries to steer file edits and command execution.

key_items.title: SkillsMetric maps static analysis detection limits
key_items.detail: Framework scores agent skill packages and identifies where malicious behaviors evade static analysis, indicating need for runtime controls.

key_items.title: ClawDojo benchmark for agent attack/defense evaluation
key_items.detail: Framework tests prompt-injection and supply-chain skill abuse against defenses using OpenClaw-style architectural attack surfaces.

categories.name: AI Governance & Trust Frameworks
categories.summary: New frameworks emerged for establishing verifiable trust in autonomous systems, including hierarchical policy composition with only-tighten rules and unified principal scoring. The focus shifted toward making drift and data leakage diagnosable through audit-friendly delegation attribution and signed recommendation verification at ingest time.

key_items.title: KYA trust layer for autonomous systems
key_items.detail: Proposes verifiable provenance and hierarchical policy composition with only-tighten rules to prevent untrusted config from silently changing agent behavior.

key_items.title: 2026 Cloud Security Report on AI transformation gaps
key_items.detail: Check Point report identifies enforcement and visibility gaps at privileged-access boundaries as GenAI workloads move to production.

categories.name: Microsoft AI Ecosystem Security
categories.summary: Dedicated resources emerged for securing Microsoft's AI ecosystem, including a community knowledge hub cataloging Copilot connectors and capabilities with associated audit queries, and practical hardening guidance for Copilot Studio deployments focusing on channel/connector restrictions and subagent inventory.

key_items.title: CopilotSec community knowledge hub launched
key_items.detail: Trust-boundary map for Copilot deployments cataloging connectors/capabilities paired with audit queries and controls for agentic flows.

key_items.title: Copilot Studio practical hardening guide
key_items.detail: Guidance on restricting channels/connectors, treating HTTP topic passthrough as attacker-influenced, and maintaining subagent inventories.

categories.name: Vulnerability Research & Advisories
categories.summary: Infrastructure-level vulnerabilities affecting AI/ML stacks were disclosed, notably the BADHOST vulnerability in Starlette affecting FastAPI, LiteLLM/vLLM, and MCP harnesses. The threat landscape digest from Check Point provided operational intelligence on AI-orchestrated abuse patterns emerging as TTPs rather than anomalies.

key_items.title: BADHOST vulnerability in Starlette disclosed
key_items.detail: Host-header handling bugs affect LLM app stacks; guidance recommends treating Host as untrusted and validating at the edge.

key_items.title: AI Threat Landscape Digest (Mar-Apr 2026)
key_items.detail: Check Point maps agentic risk to control points and tracks AI-orchestrated abuse patterns as operational TTPs.

categories.name: Standards & Frameworks
categories.summary: OWASP released crosswalks mapping the Top 10 for Agentic Applications, providing standardized risk categorization for teams building agent-based systems. This represents continued maturation of security frameworks specific to AI agent deployments.

key_items.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications crosswalks
key_items.detail: OWASP GenAI resource mapping security risks specific to agentic application architectures.

top_insights: Agent security is fundamentally a systems-security problem requiring external enforcement of least privilege, complete mediation, and instruction/data separation—not just model robustness improvements.
MCP (Model Context Protocol) has emerged as a critical attack surface with SSRF, supply chain, and connector trust boundary risks requiring end-to-end controls beyond prompt-level defenses.

Prompt injection remains highly effective across contexts from academic peer review to coding assistants, with invisible-font attacks demonstrating that input sanitization and out-of-band verification are essential.
The industry is shifting from sandboxed evaluations to real-world privilege analysis using frameworks like CIK (Capability/Identity/Knowledge) to assess agent risks under production conditions.
Static analysis alone cannot detect all malicious agent behaviors—runtime controls are necessary as research maps the detection boundaries of code scanning approaches.
